“
Our Manifesto

THE GLOBAL FAULTLINE is a digital publication exploring the faultlines beneath the headlines, from wars, politics and history to diplomatic actions, culture and controversial issues. We are building a platform and looking for curious, committed people who want to research deeply, question perspectives and help fellow readers understand the world beyond what they see online.

The world is complicated. Events of history do not stay in the past, wars are not fought overnight and today's controversies are rarely born in a vacuum. That is what inspired me to create THE GLOBAL FAULTLINE.

I wanted to build a publication that goes beyond simply telling people what happened or the current global problems. We want to look at the history behind events, the politics surrounding them, the people affected by them and the different perspectives that shape how the world understands them.

Our page will explore wars and conflicts, diplomatic actions, political controversies, history, culture and the ideas that continue to influence the world today.

TGF is being built by young people who want to understand the world rather than simply scroll past it. We won't always have the answers, and we don't intend to pretend that we do. Our goal is to research carefully, question openly and present complicated subjects in a way that makes people want to keep reading.

Viduushi Joshi
Editor-in-Chief, The Global Faultline

Editorial Team

Applications for the editorial team will be opening soon. We're looking for curious people who care about the world, ask better questions and want to help build TGF from its very first issue.

Writers Researchers Social Media Graphic Designers

Researchers

For people who genuinely enjoy knowing what is happening in the world and figuring out why.

  • Keep up with newspapers and current affairs.
  • Have strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.
  • Be comfortable reading long reports, research papers and UN documents, sometimes 100 to 200 pages or more.
  • Find, check and organise information for writers.

Writers

For curious people who know their stuff and can turn research into something people actually want to read.

  • Write clear, original and well-researched articles.
  • Have a good understanding of current affairs and be willing to learn more.
  • Find interesting angles and explain complicated topics simply.

Graphic Designers

For people who are always noticing good visuals and thinking about how things could look better.

  • Find new design ideas, concepts and inspiration.
  • Know the basics of design and be comfortable using Canva or similar tools.
  • Create graphics, covers, infographics and social-media visuals.
  • A portfolio is required.

Social Media

For people who understand social media and know how to make good work reach more people.

  • Create and edit posts, carousels, reels and other content.
  • Know the basics of editing and digital content.
  • Promote TGF and help grow its audience.
  • Keep up with trends while keeping the magazine's identity.
